definitions.explanation: An Edo-period haiku poet from Shinano (now Nagano Prefecture), usually called just {一茶|いっさ}. His haiku are plain and warm, full of sympathy for small creatures such as frogs, sparrows and flies, and for the poor and unlucky.

examples.japanese: {小林一茶|こばやしいっさ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{江戸時代|えどじだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{俳人|はいじん}→俳人：09569_haijin⟧だ。
examples.english: Kobayashi Issa was a haiku poet of the Edo period.

examples.japanese: {小林一茶|こばやしいっさ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{小|ちい}さな→小さな：02913_chiisana⟧⟦{生|い}き{物|もの}→生き物：01783_ikimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{句|く}→句：02137_ku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{詠|よ}んだ→詠む：14186_yomu⟧。
examples.english: Kobayashi Issa often wrote haiku about small creatures.

examples.japanese: 「{痩|や}せ{蛙|がえる}⟦{負|ま}ける→負ける：01134_makeru⟧な{一茶|いっさ}⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧あり」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{小林一茶|こばやしいっさ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{句|く}→句：02137_ku⟧だ。
examples.english: 'Skinny frog, don't give up — Issa is here' is a haiku by Kobayashi Issa.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
- With ⟦{松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう}→松尾芭蕉：30772_matsuobashou⟧ and {与謝蕪村|よさぶそん}, one of the three great haiku poets of the Edo period
- He wrote some 20,000 haiku, many about his own hard life

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:

- やれ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧な⟦{蠅|はえ}→蠅：05013_hae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧すり{足|あし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: don't swat it! the fly is wringing its hands and feet
